description.narrative: Support to confidence building across the Nistru river through advanced cross-river capacities for trade. 1.1: The total number of 6 Business Support Organisations (3 in TN) are engaged in capacity building activities, including advocate measures to support the business communities across the river 1.2: More than 50 companies for Transnistria region have been informed on the opportunities provided by DCFTA and technical steps needed to access EU market through 6 master classes, 4 focus groups, as well as one press club conducted. 2.1: The total number of 25 companies from Transnistria region have receive consultancy/certification support during the reporting period, in such areas as certification standards, Business model to export, Research and selection of markets for export, Export marketing and partner attraction, Sales process organization and building relationships with customers, Legal aspects and financing of export transactions, etc 2.2: 10 companies were selected for development of sales and marketing plan, as well as for the development of action plans for export development. The activities for identification of partners and export market are under way and envisage the targeted support for at least 7 companies. 2.3: 1337 (63% women) jobs maintained during the pandemic for companies participating in the Export Accelerator Initiative by providing capacity building, e-commerce, certification support to individual companies and at least 17 (>70% women) new jobs created as a result of the Small Business Support Programme implementation. 2.4: A call for application for supporting agricultural producers and processors on both banks of the river willing to join their efforts so as to penetrate new export markets or to increase their presence on the domestic and foreign markets will be launched by the end of 2020, resulting in the creation of at least 5 processing facilities 2.5 – to be reached in 2021 2.6 – The Annual Trade Forum 2020 that brings together distributors, retailers from abroad and local producers was postponed for February 2021 due to pandemic situation. In addition, the partner search and organisation of B2B meeting with distributor/retailers from the EU market with at least 4 domestic companies are under implementation and expected to finalise by end of March 2021. 3.1: 21 (>66% led by women) start-ups supported under the Small Business Support Programme, of which 16 new registered companies and other 5 young companies 3.2: more than 34 jobs maintained (>70% women) due to pandemic for the five young companies and 17 (>70% women) new jobs created as a result of equipment delivered and general and individual coaching and mentorship support programme.
